import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super(Model, self).__init__()

    def forward(self, Q: torch.Tensor, K: torch.Tensor, V: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        out = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(Q, K, V)
        return out

    V = torch.randn(batch_size, num_heads, sequence_length, embedding_dimension, device='cuda', dtype=torch.float16)

<reasoning>
The failure is a register/occupancy launch error caused by launching blocks with 1024 threads (BLOCK_M=32 warps × 32 lanes) while D=1024 forces each thread to hold two 32-element float arrays plus other locals, exceeding the register budget for 1024-thread blocks (65536/1024 = 64 regs/thread max, but kernel needs more). Reducing BLOCK_M (warps per block) reduces threads/block, which increases the register/thread cap, without changing any of the kernel's algorithm, memory layout, or math. Since N=256, BLOCK_M=8 divides evenly (256/8=32 blocks per batch-head), and 8*32=256 threads/block gives up to 65536/256=256 regs/thread, comfortably fitting the register footprint required by D=1024.

This is a pure launch-configuration change: the kernel body already computes BLOCK_M dynamically from blockDim.x/32, so lowering the host constant is sufficient and preserves the custom CUTE flash-attention structure exactly.
</reasoning>
